name: Garrison of Fort Morgan (Alabama troops pending transfer)
proposed_strength: 9 full companies plus 46 men of a tenth (4 Apr); inferred 500-900 men; 400-500 in early Jan

strength_sources: OR I-52 pt 2 pp.34-35 (Jere. Clemens, Mobile, 4 Apr 1861: Hardee "has now at Fort Morgan nine full companies of volunteers and forty-six men of another company" as printed; "about 88 men" as printed after "when it is filled", likely a cut-off figure such as 880; the OCR is unclear); OR I-1 p.330 (Lt C. B. Reese to Totten: "at least 400 and perhaps 500 men", seizure of the fort, early Jan, no date on the page; about 30 men to remain); OR I-52 pt 2 p.47 (J. T. Repo notes already hold the 28 Mar A&IG 'at least 400' (OR IV-1 pp.192-193; not re-read). Hardee's later (13 Apr, OR I-52 pt 2 p.45) three more companies from Mount Vernon.

name: Texas State mounted regiment (Col. John S. Ford): Rio Grande

name: Fort Monroe garrison (Artillery School)
strength_sources: OR III-1 p.23 (distribution, Fort Monroe: A and C 1st Art; B and L 2nd; F and K 3rd; D and L 4th; A moved Jan 24; two readings agree); OR I-1 p.352 (Dimick, 22-23 Jan: 40 men detached to Co A); OR I-2 p.641 (Scott, May 1861: "seven companies of regular artillery" per paraphrase, no date visible, letter heading May 18 follows); OR III-1 p.22 (yardsticks); OR I-51 pt 1 p.315 (Holt to Tredway, 27 Feb 1861: a company was withdrawn from Fort Monroe weeks earlier)
strength_notes: basis: 7 companies (8 on 1 Jan less A/1st Art, left 24 Jan). Present: 7 x 59.5 = 416 men, less 40 men detached to Vogdes on 22 Jan (OR I-1 p.352) = 376, plus officers 7 x 1.9 = about 13, gives about 390. Rolls: 7 x 61.6 = 431 less 40 = 391, plus officers 7 x 3.75 = 26, about 417. Band widened for company-size variation and for the School's staff and band. No Fort Monroe return found. Dimick's 10 May report (spirit61, OR I-2) gives no troop count; OR I-2 p.612 (Townsend to Dimick, 30 Apr) gives none for the garrison. The F/K 3rd Art vs I/3rd conflict: both readings of p.23 give F and K; the Army Register not consulted. Scott's 24 Jan memo (OR I-51 pt 1 p.312) proposed drawing "four or five companies" from Fort Monroe: p.23 shows no such move, so I take it as not executed (p.23 layout of "Do." lines is uncertain). Late May figure for comparison: Encyclopedia Virginia, about 4,500 by end of May (secondary, after the window)

name: Key West garrison (Brannan)

name: Marine guard, Philadelphia Navy Yard
strength_sources: NavyReg1861 pp.76-80 (stations listed: HQ and Washington, Philadelphia, Brooklyn, Portsmouth NH, Charlestown, Gosport, Warrington; fetch via archive.org full text of registerofcom18601862wash, 1861 portion at roughly 700,000-800,000 characters); ORN I-4 pp.283-284 via the repo, not re-read

Upper bound is a judgment: Navy Register 1861 pp.76-80 shows at Philadelphia one marine officer plus a recruiting rendezvous (read by paraphrase; names not matched to stations), i.e. a guard commanded by one captain; Pensacola yard guard 38 (snippet-unverified, see below) is the only other station figure. NO station return found. The Marine Corps History Division pamphlet and the Winter 2021 article that may carry the 2 Nov 1860 Adjutant and Inspector's report returned 403: not routed around. Zeilin named at Philadelphia in the repo from NavyReg1861 p.99; I could not match the register's marine entries by name

name: Marine Corps headquarters and barracks, Washington
strength_sources: NavyReg1861 pp.76-80 (several officers at Washington); OR I-51 pt 1 pp.312-314 (Toucey 28 Jan; Harris 18 Jan; Taylor 16 Jan; Scott order of 12 Feb telling Harris to send "as many as he can spare" to the Capitol: no number); ORN I-4 pp.263, 285, 292 via the repo
strength_notes: basis: Low bound 100 detailed for the Pawnee on 19 Apr (ORN I-4 p.285, via the repo) + 34 to Norfolk 20 Apr (ORN I-4 p.292, via the repo) + 20 marines put aboard the Anacostia in April (historycentral.com April 1861 chronology, secondary, snippet) = 154. High bound 400 from "300 to 400 marines at the barracks" in search summaries of secondary accounts (Wikipedia mirror and a barracks-history page; not the primary): snippet-unverified. Also in January 40 marines went to Fort Washington (Capt Taylor, 5 Jan) and 30 to Fort McHenry (9 Jan) from the barracks (secondary chronology; OR I-51 pt 1 p.313 confirms Taylor commanded marines at Fort Washington on 16 Jan, and the Navy Dept's 15-day detail). No return. Corps total for context (not a station figure): 1,775 on 2 Nov 1860 = 63 officers + 252 NCOs + 113 musicians + 1,347 privates (arithmetic checks); Marine Corps History 2021 article via a search summary, which cites the Navy Secretary's 1860 report in the President's message (vol. 3, pp. 382-85 per the summary): snippet-unverified. The 1861 Navy Register has no marine headcount (checked: its pay table and officer lists only). Pensacola yard: 38 marines under Capt Josiah Watson at the 12 Jan 1861 surrender (secondary chronology via search summary; the chronology page itself returned 410): snippet-unverified. Landed at Fort Pickens 12 Apr: 110 marines with Vogdes (OR I-1 p.395, via the earlier helper). Warfare History Network "four companies of eighty" in July is after the window

name: Regulars in the Department of New Mexico
strength_quality: inferred (company count read from OCR; per-company yardstick Dec 1860); one return outside the window (30 Jun)
strength_sources: OR III-1 p.26 (distribution, Dept of New Mexico, 1 Jan to 15 Apr 1861; two readings, OCR flags on dates); OR III-1 p.22; OR III-1 p.301 (Abstract of returns, Dept of New Mexico, 30 Jun 1861: 54 officers, 1,464 men present for duty, aggregate present 1,941, present and absent 2,466; read by the earlier helper; I did not re-fetch p.301); OR I-1 p.599 (Loring 23 Mar: no figure)
strength_notes: basis: 36 companies on 5 Mar (39 on 1 Jan less E, B, K of 8th Inf gone to Texas by 21 Feb): Dragoons 4 (2nd: G, I; 1st: D, G), Mounted Rifles 10, 5th Inf 10, 7th Inf 10, 10th Inf 2. Present: cavalry-type 14 x 62.5 = 875, infantry 22 x 71.4 = 1,571, officers 36 x 1.9 = 68, total about 2,510. Rolls: 14 x 72.1 = 1,009 + 22 x 78.5 = 1,727 + officers 36 x 3.75 = 135, total about 2,870. Low bound is the 30 Jun return itself (aggregate present 1,941): net decline from the Dec 1860 per-company norm (officer resignations, desertion, detachments) is unexplained. No Jan or Feb 1861 return found in OR I-4 pp.1-100 or elsewhere (search found only the 31 Dec 1861 return at OR I-4 p.81). Present-for-duty equivalent: 78 percent of aggregate present at 30 Jun, so about 1,500 to 1,950 on 5 Mar. Detached companies on 5 Mar are not stated. Conflict: arithmetic present (2,510) vs the 30 Jun aggregate present (1,941) differ by 23 percent

name: Regulars in the Department of the Pacific
strength_quality: inferred plus one return outside the window (June)
strength_sources: OR III-1 pp.24 (Dept of Oregon and Dept of California, 1 Jan to 15 Apr 1861; two readings); OR III-1 p.22; OR I-50 pt 1 p.525 (Abstract from return of the Department of the Pacific, Sumner, month of June 1861: HQ 18 officers and 1 man; District of Oregon 31 / 488 / 701 / 974; troops in California and Nevada 65 / 1,575 / 2,085 / 2,367; total 114 / 2,064 / 2,805 / 3,361; columns reconstructed from fragments)
strength_notes: basis: About 45 companies on 5 Mar (my counts 43-46): Oregon and Washington about 26 (3rd Art A, B, C, D, G, L, M; 1st Dragoons C, E, H, I; 4th Inf A, C, F, G, H, K; 9th Inf A, B, C, D, E, F, H, I and one more at Colville), California and Nevada about 19 (3rd Art H; 1st Dragoons A, B, F, K; 4th Inf B, D, E, I; 6th Inf A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, K). A and B 3rd Art moved Vancouver to Fort Point 28 Feb to 5 Mar. Present: artillery 8 x 59.5 = 476, dragoons 8 x 62.5 = 500, infantry 29 x 71.4 = 2,071, plus officers 85, total about 3,130. Rolls: 8 x 61.6 + 8 x 72.1 + 29 x 78.5 = 3,347 men + officers 169 = about 3,516. June return: aggregate present 2,805; rolls 3,361. Band low is June aggregate present, high is the Dec-norm present. The two departments merged as the Department of the Pacific on 15 Jan 1861 (OR I-50 pt 1 p.1 chronology as reported in a search summary). No Jan to Apr abstract found (OR I-50 pt 1 p.2 is a chronology starting 14 Apr). Present for duty on 30 Jun: 2,178 (114 + 2,064), about 78 percent of aggregate present, so about 2,100 to 2,450 on 5 Mar on that measure. By June the District of Oregon was already down to 488 men present (aggregate 701): the June return understates March. A search summary giving 3,382 for 15 Jan: snippet-unverified, a close fit to the rolls band (3,361 to 3,516) and probably the same measure. The Dept of the Pacific plan of Sumner in April (400 to Alcatraz, 150 to Fort Point): OR I-50 pt 1 p.472, via earlier helper

name: Fort Pickens garrison
stores_basis: stated "provisions for five months for my present command" x 30 (`computed` conversion)
stores_sources: OR I-1 p.341 (Slemmer to Cooper, 5 Feb 1861)
stores_notes: Repository value confirmed and the report is dated 5 Feb. Later qualitative evidence says the 150 does not carry to 5 March: 18 Mar "recommend that subsistence stores be sent immediately" and the contractor stopped beef (pp.361-362); 30 Mar "Fresh provisions are now denied us" (p.365); 12 Apr Slemmer asks that provisions be landed (p.388); 17-19 Apr Brown found "the subsistence nearly exhausted" (pp.380-381). Vogdes's own supplies were landed here (see next row).

name: Company A, 1st Artillery (Vogdes), afloat
strength_sources: OR I-1 p.352 (Dimick, order 22-23 Jan: the 40 men, three months' provisions); OR I-1 p.353 (Dimick 25 Jan: a return of Vogdes's command enclosed, not printed); OR I-1 pp.357-358 (Vogdes 7 Feb, per a jfepperson.org page: Slemmer's command "forty-six enlisted men for duty" plus about 30 sailors; no number for Co A); OR I-1 p.378 (Vogdes landing: no count)
strength_notes: basis: Company A, 1st Artillery was "filled to maximum" by 40 attached men (5, 6, 6, 6, 5, 6, 6 from C/1st, B/2nd, L/2nd, F/3rd, K/3rd, D/4th, L/4th). Maximum in law: 74 privates (9 Stat. 439) plus non-privates (not sourced for the regular service; the 22 July 1861 volunteer act, printed in the Regulations appendix, gives 1 first sergeant, 4 sergeants, 8 corporals, 2 musicians, 1 wagoner, a proxy of 16) = about 90. Cross-check: company average 59.5 + 40 attached = about 99. The company return of 25 Jan 1861 exists but is not printed. Total of company plus attached men is not stated anywhere I read. Vogdes's own estimate: his company, the marines and sailors would bring the garrison to 400 (target, not a count). 110 marines landed with him on 12 Apr (OR I-1 p.395, prior helper) are not part of this block. The block is aboard the USS Brooklyn on 5 March (the landing was not until 12 April)
stores_sources: OR I-1 p.353 (order to Vogdes) and p.351 (Thomas to Dimick: "not exceeding four months' supply")
stores_notes: Confirmed. NEW: ORN I-4 p.97 (Adams, 18 Mar 1861): the Brooklyn's soldiers' "own supplies having been landed ... at Fort Pickens" (the greater part), so by mid-March they were living on ship's rations and their 90 days is mostly ashore in the fort, not with the company afloat. The lead should not count it twice with Pickens.

name: Troops at the Saint Louis Arsenal
strength_quality: return (dated two weeks before the snapshot)
strength_sources: OR I-1 p.654 (Harney to Thomas, 19 Feb: "three hundred recruits", "nine officers and four hundred and eighty-four men", read in two fetches); OR I-1 p.655 (Hagner to Craig, 21 Feb: aggregate 488; reinforcements 16 Feb 3 officers + 200 men, 19 Feb 1 officer + 101 men, per the earlier helper; not re-fetched); OR I-1 pp.657-658 (Lyon's command from 13 Mar by SO 74; ordnance men not part of it; Hagner protests; no numbers); OR I-3 p.4 (Lyon 11 May: 3,436 reserve corps men sworn in on 7-8 May, not the regular garrison)
strength_notes: basis: Hagner's own aggregate on 21 Feb is 488; Harney on 19 Feb gives 9 officers and 484 men (= 493). About 300 of these are recruits from Jefferson Barracks; Lyon's company of the 2nd Infantry arrived earlier and is not given separately. No 4-5 March count found. If the recruits left before March the figure would be far lower: the only company figure is "just over 60 men per company" for the two regular companies before Camp Jackson, in a secondary article seen in a search summary (snippet-unverified), so a floor of about 60 plus Hagner's ordnance detachment. Harney's 493 vs Hagner's 488: different dates (19 vs 21 Feb), 5 apart, both returns by the same post

name: Fort Sumter garrison
stores_basis: stated ("about one week longer" if the laborers are sent away)
stores_sources: OR I-1 p.230 (Anderson to Thomas, 1 Apr 1861)
stores_notes: Repository's 7 is confirmed. Band from the same pages: "4 to 5 days" of bread (p.232, 3 Apr); "after the 10th" on short allowance (p.230); about 35 days "comfortable subsistence" in Hall's A.A.C.S. note (p.231) which is ambiguous; Fox's information, through the 15th (p.235). Hall's ration counts (1,467 pork, 3,485 flour, etc.) give a command of 90 persons/day (`computed`).
